questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What is the primary purpose of establishing indications before performing an echocardiogram?
options: Improve patient care and clinical outcomes
questions.explanation: A valid indication ties the study to a clinical question. The point of imaging is to improve patient care and outcomes — not to generate images for their own sake. *(Practice review slide 3.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  According to Otto, the usefulness of an echocardiographic examination is best measured by:. Which answer is most accurate?
questions.explanation: Otto frames the value of any test by its effect on the patient's clinical outcome — does it change management and improve care? *(Practice review slide 5.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  A patient presents with newly developed exertional dyspnea. What is the most appropriate next step?
questions.explanation: Before imaging, assess whether echo is appropriate for this presentation. Exertional dyspnea is a recognized indication, but appropriateness still drives the decision. *(Practice review slide 7.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  Which condition represents a common indication for echocardiography?
questions.explanation: The course review identifies Migraine headaches as the correct response. *(Practice review slide 9.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  A patient with known valvular disease is referred for follow-up. Which principle supports repeat echocardiography?
questions.explanation: Repeat imaging in KNOWN valvular disease is justified as disease monitoring — tracking severity and the ventricle's response over time. *(Practice review slide 11.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  Which category of disease is commonly evaluated using echocardiography?
questions.explanation: Cardiomyopathy is a core echo target — echo assesses chamber size, wall thickness, and systolic and diastolic function. *(Practice review slide 13.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  Symptoms such as dyspnea, chest pain, and syncope are considered:. Which answer is most accurate?
questions.explanation: The course review identifies Symptom-based indications as the correct response. *(Practice review slide 15.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  Which patient presentation is most likely to justify an echocardiogram?
questions.explanation: The course review identifies New onset heart failure symptoms as the correct response. *(Practice review slide 17.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  A patient with suspected infective endocarditis is referred for imaging. This indication aligns with:. Which answer is most accurate?
questions.explanation: Suspected infective endocarditis is a recognized indication; among these options it maps to the indication category (expanded / special indications). *(Practice review slide 19.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  One of the most important factors pertaining to good patient outcomes is:. Which answer is most accurate?
options: Expertise of the Sonographer and interpreting physician
Knowledge of pathology and requirement of exam expansion
questions.explanation: The expertise of the sonographer and interpreting physician is foundational — skilled acquisition and interpretation underpin every downstream measurement and decision. *(Practice review slide 21.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  An important part of providing a reliable examination result is having the knowledge and skill to compensate and respond for:. Which answer is most accurate?
questions.explanation: Reliable results require recognizing and compensating for limitations — poor acoustic windows, body habitus, artifacts, and incomplete data. *(Practice review slide 23.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  Peer review supports:. Which answer is most accurate?
questions.explanation: Peer review feeds continuous quality improvement — comparing findings, catching discrepancies, and refining practice over time. *(Practice review slide 25.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  Image quality, protocol adherence and equipment maintenance are components of:. Which answer is most accurate?
questions.explanation: These are core components of Quality Assurance — the systems that keep studies accurate and reproducible. *(Practice review slide 27.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  Accuracy, consistency and structured reports ensure:. Which answer is most accurate?
questions.explanation: Accurate, consistent, structured reports define reporting quality — the report is the study's clinical deliverable. *(Practice review slide 29.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  Missed pathology most directly impacts:. Which answer is most accurate?
questions.explanation: Missed pathology directly degrades diagnostic quality — the study has failed its core purpose of detecting disease. *(Practice review slide 31.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  Clinical integration in echocardiography combines:. Which answer is most accurate?
questions.explanation: Clinical integration brings together indications, Appropriate Use Criteria, and QA — the right test, chosen well, performed and reported to standard. *(Practice review slide 33.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  The most appropriate overall approach to echocardiography practice is to:. Which answer is most accurate?
options: Use echo appropriately and apply QA standards
questions.explanation: Best practice is to use echo appropriately (right indication and AUC) and apply QA standards throughout. *(Practice review slide 35.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  QA is a responsibility of:. Which answer is most accurate?
questions.explanation: QA is a front-line responsibility of sonographers — the person acquiring the images is the first guardian of study quality. *(Practice review slide 37.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  The ASE Appropriate Use Criteria were developed to support:. Which answer is most accurate?
questions.explanation: The ASE Appropriate Use Criteria ensure echo is used where it benefits patients — improving care while reducing low-value testing and cost. *(Practice review slide 39.)*

questions.stem: An adult cardiac sonography student is interpreting a teaching case.  A patient with known valvular disease is referred for follow-up. Which principle supports repeat echocardiography?
questions.explanation: Repeat imaging in KNOWN valvular disease is justified as disease monitoring — tracking severity and the ventricle's response over time. *(Practice review slide 11.)*

questions.stem: An adult cardiac sonography student is interpreting a teaching case.  Which category of disease is commonly evaluated using echocardiography?
questions.explanation: Cardiomyopathy is a core echo target — echo assesses chamber size, wall thickness, and systolic and diastolic function. *(Practice review slide 13.)*

questions.stem: An adult cardiac sonography student is interpreting a teaching case.  Symptoms such as dyspnea, chest pain, and syncope are considered:. Which answer is most accurate?
questions.explanation: The course review identifies Symptom-based indications as the correct response. *(Practice review slide 15.)*

questions.stem: An adult cardiac sonography student is interpreting a teaching case.  Which patient presentation is most likely to justify an echocardiogram?
questions.explanation: The course review identifies New onset heart failure symptoms as the correct response. *(Practice review slide 17.)*

questions.stem: An adult cardiac sonography student is interpreting a teaching case.  A patient with suspected infective endocarditis is referred for imaging. This indication aligns with:. Which answer is most accurate?
questions.explanation: Suspected infective endocarditis is a recognized indication; among these options it maps to the indication category (expanded / special indications). *(Practice review slide 19.)*

questions.stem: An adult cardiac sonography student is interpreting a teaching case.  One of the most important factors pertaining to good patient outcomes is:. Which answer is most accurate?
options: Knowledge of pathology and requirement of exam expansion
Expertise of the Sonographer and interpreting physician
questions.explanation: The expertise of the sonographer and interpreting physician is foundational — skilled acquisition and interpretation underpin every downstream measurement and decision. *(Practice review slide 21.)*

questions.stem: An adult cardiac sonography student is interpreting a teaching case.  An important part of providing a reliable examination result is having the knowledge and skill to compensate and respond for:. Which answer is most accurate?
questions.explanation: Reliable results require recognizing and compensating for limitations — poor acoustic windows, body habitus, artifacts, and incomplete data. *(Practice review slide 23.)*

questions.stem: An adult cardiac sonography student is interpreting a teaching case.  Peer review supports:. Which answer is most accurate?
questions.explanation: Peer review feeds continuous quality improvement — comparing findings, catching discrepancies, and refining practice over time. *(Practice review slide 25.)*

questions.stem: An adult cardiac sonography student is interpreting a teaching case.  Image quality, protocol adherence and equipment maintenance are components of:. Which answer is most accurate?
questions.explanation: These are core components of Quality Assurance — the systems that keep studies accurate and reproducible. *(Practice review slide 27.)*

questions.stem: An adult cardiac sonography student is interpreting a teaching case.  Accuracy, consistency and structured reports ensure:. Which answer is most accurate?
questions.explanation: Accurate, consistent, structured reports define reporting quality — the report is the study's clinical deliverable. *(Practice review slide 29.)*

questions.stem: An adult cardiac sonography student is interpreting a teaching case.  Missed pathology most directly impacts:. Which answer is most accurate?
questions.explanation: Missed pathology directly degrades diagnostic quality — the study has failed its core purpose of detecting disease. *(Practice review slide 31.)*

questions.stem: An adult cardiac sonography student is interpreting a teaching case.  Clinical integration in echocardiography combines:. Which answer is most accurate?
questions.explanation: Clinical integration brings together indications, Appropriate Use Criteria, and QA — the right test, chosen well, performed and reported to standard. *(Practice review slide 33.)*

questions.stem: An adult cardiac sonography student is interpreting a teaching case.  The most appropriate overall approach to echocardiography practice is to:. Which answer is most accurate?
options: Use echo appropriately and apply QA standards
questions.explanation: Best practice is to use echo appropriately (right indication and AUC) and apply QA standards throughout. *(Practice review slide 35.)*

questions.stem: An adult cardiac sonography student is interpreting a teaching case.  QA is a responsibility of:. Which answer is most accurate?
questions.explanation: QA is a front-line responsibility of sonographers — the person acquiring the images is the first guardian of study quality. *(Practice review slide 37.)*

questions.stem: An adult cardiac sonography student is interpreting a teaching case.  The ASE Appropriate Use Criteria were developed to support:. Which answer is most accurate?
questions.explanation: The ASE Appropriate Use Criteria ensure echo is used where it benefits patients — improving care while reducing low-value testing and cost. *(Practice review slide 39.)*

questions.stem: An adult cardiac sonography student is interpreting a teaching case.  In diagnostic imaging, the person who oversees the quality assurance processes, compliance, auditing, performance improvement and metrics is the:. Which answer is most accurate?
questions.explanation: The Quality Assurance Coordinator oversees QA processes, compliance, auditing, performance improvement, and metrics. *(Practice review slide 41.)*

questions.stem: Before image acquisition, a sonographer checks their understanding of the following.  What is the primary purpose of establishing indications before performing an echocardiogram?
options: Improve patient care and clinical outcomes
